title: Nonenzymatic Protein Function and Protein Analysis
scopeNote: Original condensed MCAT biochemistry lessons covering the declared outline sections. This release is implemented, not independently scientifically verified; it is not exhaustive textbook coverage.

steps.text: Proteins provide structural support, transport cargo, generate force and bind signals as well as catalyze reactions. Function depends on conformation and context.
Hemoglobin carries oxygen with cooperative subunit interactions. Myoglobin is a monomeric oxygen-binding protein whose binding curve is typically hyperbolic.
Actin and myosin participate in force generation. A motor converts chemical energy into directed mechanical work rather than producing energy from nothing.
Binding affinity and transport capacity are distinct. A change that shifts oxygen affinity need not change the number of available binding sites.

steps.text: A signaling ligand binds a receptor, which changes downstream activity. Receptor occupancy and the magnitude of a cell response are related but not identical.
A G-protein pathway can amplify signaling through second messengers. GTP hydrolysis helps switch a G protein off; amplification does not imply an unlimited response.
Receptor tyrosine kinases often signal through ligand-induced association and phosphorylation. Intracellular receptors can regulate transcription after binding permeant ligands.
Desensitization and feedback restrain responses. Distinguish a binding defect from a downstream relay defect by testing both ligand binding and cell output.

steps.text: Purification separates proteins using different properties. A crude mixture can be fractionated before a more selective step; yield and purity must be tracked separately.
In size-exclusion chromatography, larger species generally elute earlier because they enter fewer pores. This ordering differs from migration through an SDS gel.
Ion exchange separates by charge at the chosen pH. A positively charged anion-exchange resin binds negatively charged analytes; salt or pH changes can elute them.
Affinity purification uses a specific binding interaction. Strong binding to a ligand does not establish catalytic activity; assay the fractions to locate active protein.

steps.text: SDS-PAGE denatures proteins and gives a roughly uniform negative charge-to-mass ratio, so separation primarily reflects polypeptide size. Smaller chains usually migrate farther.
Reducing SDS-PAGE can separate chains linked by disulfides. Nonreducing conditions preserve those disulfide links but still disrupt many noncovalent associations.
Isoelectric focusing separates proteins according to pI in a pH gradient. Native electrophoresis depends on charge, size and shape together.
A band demonstrates staining of material, not necessarily biological function. Pair electrophoretic evidence with an activity assay when assessing active enzyme recovery.
